implementation_summary: ADR 0037: Accepted 2026-11-03 (DEC-001; D-004/Q-51 closed-default; D-005/Q-55 allow-helpers). It records six access levels that match AuditAccess in AUDIT_API. Owner means whoever holds the access key. A Helper gets view, edit or export only on the Website Audits given to them, and never passes an owner row. The only public rows are Shared Links. Dispatch refuses a route with no declared access, or with an unknown one. The beta policy is also closed by default: beta visitors reach only public Shared Link routes, plus the Helper sign-in routes and the routes of Website Audits given to a Helper who has a valid Helper session. Every other audit route stays closed in beta. The ADR links ADR 0027, 0033 and 0036. Helper sign-in is placed here; Google ID token verification is left to the REQ-033 task, which extends this ADR instead of writing another 0037. ADR 0015: Status is now 'Accepted for pacing only' (Q-12, ADR 0033): one request at a time per host and robots.txt Crawl-delay honoured, covering top-level requests only (Q-56 default), built by BE-105. GraphQL query POSTs and GET/HEAD replay stay undecided, and the Safety Filter rules are unchanged. Added a docs contract test that follows the style of adr-0036.test.ts. It reads the AuditAccess levels from website-audit.ts, so the ADR and the type cannot drift apart.

risks: ADR 0015 says the pacing is 'built by task BE-105'. BE-105 is still PENDING in engineering/plan.md, so the decision is recorded but not yet implemented.

ADR 0037 names authorizeRoute (BE-102) as the single enforcement point, and says handlers also check the Helper grant on the Website Audit in the request (:id), to block access to other audits by changing the id. BE-102 and the REQ-033 task must follow this.

ADR 0037 defines the owner as the access-key holder, or a local request when no access key is set, which matches the runner's current behaviour. A reviewer should confirm this is the intended local-mode rule.
The test runner printed a stray line, "'JS' is not recognized as an internal or external command", from the shell or pnpm wrapper. It did not affect the result.
handoff: BE-102: give every Route an access level (one of six, equal to AUDIT_API[*].access) and a beta policy, both closed by default. In beta, allow only public routes, Helper sign-in routes, and view/edit/export routes for a Helper with a valid session on a Website Audit given to them. REQ-033 task: add the Google ID token verification details (audience, issuer, expiry, session cookie) to ADR 0037; do not create a new ADR number. ADR 0033's follow-up list already points to 0037.
